problem_statement: When a TCP connection receives a FIN packet that simultaneously acknowledges the most recently sent data, the stack fails to update its outstanding-send bookkeeping correctly. As a result, the FIN,ACK reply that the stack sends back carries an inflated sequence number (it adds the still-unacknowledged data length on top of the already-advanced send pointer), instead of the next expected sequence number. A peer that has just acknowledged the last data in its FIN should see a FIN,ACK reply whose sequence number equals its own expected next sequence, so the connection closes cleanly with correct sequence numbers.
twister_command: scripts/twister -p native_sim/native/64 -T tests/net/tcp -s tests/net/tcp/net.tcp.simple -s net.tcp.simple -O twister-out --no-clean -W
